lines.text: Can brake fluid free a rusted bolt better than the stuff that's made for it?
He rusts a pile of bolts on purpose and drips six fluids on them.
The trick is capillary action which pulls a thin liquid into tiny gaps like a paper towel drinking a spill.
The brake fluid just sits on the washer like it gave up.
But when he cuts the bolt open it crept all the way to the bottom.
Fluid Film coats everything like slime but it's too thick to squeeze into the threads.
Then viewers beg him to mix them all into one super oil which is risky because chemicals can react.
And the mix never crept down so a nut that was only hand tight needed 56 foot pounds.
The winner is Seafoam Deep Creep with CRC Knocker Loose right behind it.
Because in rusty threads the gaps are microscopic so only the thinnest fluid gets in.
So would you trust brake fluid on your next rusted bolt?
